edges.description: Bacteria that reach a neonatal barrier site must survive serum complement to expand in blood.
Serum-resistant organisms persist in blood long enough to amplify and reach the neonatal blood-brain barrier.
Bloodborne organisms engage endothelial OmpA-Ecgp96 and CNF1-37LRP receptors to initiate barrier invasion.
edges.target: OmpA- and CNF1-Driven HBMEC Invasion Signaling

edges.description: Bloodborne IbeA+ organisms engage endothelial vimentin to invade the barrier.
Low-iron blood conditions activate the CsiR/IlvB endothelial invasion route.
Sustained high-grade bacteremia produces systemic fever.
Infected endothelial cells internalize and translocate organisms across the blood-brain barrier toward cerebrospinal fluid.
edges.source: OmpA- and CNF1-Driven HBMEC Invasion Signaling

edges.description: RS218 infection of brain microvascular endothelial cells assembles the Ripoptosome death complex.
edges.source: OmpA- and CNF1-Driven HBMEC Invasion Signaling

edges.description: Vimentin-dependent invasion contributes to translocation of organisms across the barrier toward cerebrospinal fluid.
Low-iron-induced FAK/PI3K signaling and actin remodeling promote penetration of the barrier toward cerebrospinal fluid.
Barrier crossing places organisms in the cerebrospinal-fluid compartment that supports bacterial replication.
Endothelial infection and CSF bacterial products stimulate leukocyte trafficking across brain endothelial cells.
Neutrophil influx amplifies cytokine release and brain injury in the neonatal meningeal compartment.
Barrier disruption allows bacterial invasion and inflammatory injury to spread into neonatal brain tissue.
Cortical irritation from neonatal meningitis and brain injury produces seizures.
Severe neuroinflammation and brain injury depress consciousness to coma.
Raised intracranial pressure from meningeal inflammation bulges the fontanelle.
Meningeal inflammation produces nuchal rigidity.
Inflammatory injury to the auditory pathway produces sensorineural hearing loss as a long-term sequela.
Neonatal brain injury produces neurodevelopmental impairment as a long-term sequela.
Focal suppuration in the neonatal brain produces cerebral abscess.
Spread of infection to the ventricular lining produces ventriculitis.
Barrier injury and vascular compromise produce ischaemo-haemorrhagic cerebral lesions.
The model requires E. coli K1 factors needed for systemic dissemination before brain infection and can test antibody-mediated PNAG protection.
edges.limitations: The system uses experimentally infected neonatal mice, so it does not reproduce natural human maternal delivery or nosocomial acquisition.
edges.source: Neonatal mouse E. coli K1 PNAG immunization model

edges.description: Direct ventricular inoculation isolates CSF replication and inflammatory neonatal brain injury from the antecedent bacteremia and barrier-crossing phases.
edges.limitations: The model bypasses maternal acquisition, bacteremia, and natural blood-brain-barrier invasion by injecting bacteria directly into the ventricle.
edges.source: Newborn rat intraventricular E. coli meningitis model
